description: The World Register of Dams is the International Commission on Large Dams' global database of large dams, developed since 1958 and maintained by its Technical Committee on the World Register of Dams and Documentation from information supplied mostly by ICOLD national committees. The September 2025 edition covers 62,362 dams meeting ICOLD's definition of a large dam: at least 15 metres high, or 5 to 15 metres high impounding more than 3 million cubic metres. Records give country, dam type, height, reservoir capacity, purposes such as irrigation, hydropower, water supply, flood control and tailings, installed capacity and other fields chosen in a query builder, and results can be exported as CSV or PDF. A free general synthesis page summarises the register by country, height, type, reservoir capacity, age and purpose; searching the register itself needs a personal access code from ICOLD, and the page does not publish price or reuse terms. Caveats: ICOLD states it cannot guarantee completeness or accuracy, the purpose field is filled for only 42,274 dams, and the page does not mention coordinates, so spatial work usually pairs it with georeferenced sets. Simulation uses: building dam and reservoir inventories for dam-break hazard exposure, reservoir capacity planning and cascading failure between water, flood defence and hydropower systems. Related records: the US National Inventory of Dams (data-usace-national-inventory-of-dams) and FAO AQUASTAT georeferenced dams (data-fao-aquastat-georeferenced-dams) cover overlapping assets with locations.
